title: Guacharaca (notched tube)
summary: The guacharaca is a scraped idiophone made of a grooved palm-wood tube scraped with a three-pronged fork, used in vallenato. The player rubs the fork along the notches to make a dry, scratchy rhythm.
howToPlay: Four places are lit along the tube: Down and Up scrapes, Scratch in the middle, Knock at the lower end.
The fork rides the grooves as each stroke sounds; the grooves it crosses gleam.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Keep the scrape dry and steady.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: In vallenato from the Caribbean coast of Colombia it sits with the box drum and the accordion, giving the music a dry, scratchy edge.
credits: Tradition: the guacharaca; patterns written for this game
